frameworkMetadata.description: Defines revenue motion and industry-specific contextual intelligence required by the RevOS Pipeline Assessment Engine to evaluate opportunity winability, identify risks, recommend improvement actions, and continuously adapt assessment reasoning based on business context. Version 1.1 adds canonical, evidence-driven SWOT and TOWS intelligence configuration through universal, revenue-motion, and industry inheritance layers.

configurationPrinciples.description: The eight PADF dimensions remain universal across all industries and revenue motions. Configuration modifies interpretation and priority but never changes the assessment ontology.
Pipeline behavior is primarily influenced by the selling motion. Industry configuration is applied within the context of the revenue motion.
Industry profiles adapt evidence expectations, risk patterns, and reasoning guidance without creating new assessment dimensions.
All assessment conclusions, risk identification, and recommendations must be traceable to available evidence.
Configuration provides contextual reasoning guidance to AI engines rather than replacing AI judgment with static scoring rules.
Pipeline assessment must support continuous reassessment as new evidence, events, and customer interactions occur.

framework_definition.framework_purpose: Provide evidence-driven SWOT and TOWS intelligence for Pipeline Assessment by identifying and evaluating opportunity-specific internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats, then translating relevant factor combinations into actionable winning-strategy inputs.
framework_scope: Universal SWOT factor taxonomy and baseline factor configurations
Revenue-motion-specific SWOT factor and evaluation overrides for all six supported revenue motion families
Industry-specific SWOT factor and evaluation overrides for all 16 supported industry profiles
Evidence provenance, quality, confidence, and gap management
TOWS strategy generation and integration with the existing Winning Strategy engine
Continuous factor and strategy reassessment with traceability

analytical_boundaries.internal_factor_definition: Strengths and weaknesses describe the seller's own capabilities, assets, relationships, proof, positioning, resources, and execution in the specific opportunity; they are not customer attributes.
analytical_boundaries.external_factor_definition: Opportunities and threats describe external customer, market, competitive, procurement, regulatory, funding, timing, or operating conditions relevant to the opportunity.
analytical_boundaries.padf_relationship: SWOT factors may map contextually to one or more of the eight universal PADF dimensions through non-exclusive many-to-many references. SWOT does not create, rename, replace, or reweight the PADF ontology itself.
analytical_boundaries.risk_intelligence_relationship: SWOT threats and weaknesses may cross-reference existing RiskIntelligence records where relevant. The SWOT layer remains complementary and must avoid creating duplicate risk records; shared evidence references are allowed.
analytical_boundaries.winning_strategy_relationship: Relevant TOWS combinations produce structured strategy inputs for the existing WinningStrategyRecommendationConfigurations and Winning Strategy engine. SWOT does not create a parallel winning-strategy engine.

evaluation_overrides.scoring_guidance: Evaluate each factor independently on the defined dimensions. Do not calculate or imply a universal composite SWOT score. Keep strategic impact distinct from evidence confidence.
evaluation_overrides.priority_guidance: Prioritize materiality to winability, evidence confidence, urgency, manageability, and the seller's ability to influence the outcome.

SO.strategic_logic: Use substantiated internal strengths to capture a relevant external customer or market opportunity.
SO.primary_objective: Convert proven capability and customer value into a differentiated, customer-validated path to selection.

WO.strategic_logic: Address a material internal weakness so the opportunity can be pursued credibly.
WO.primary_objective: Close evidence, capability, stakeholder, or execution gaps that currently prevent the opportunity from being converted.

ST.strategic_logic: Use substantiated internal strengths to mitigate or neutralize an external threat.
ST.primary_objective: Apply proven differentiation, relationships, technical capability, or delivery evidence to reduce competitive or buying-process exposure.

WT.strategic_logic: Reduce exposure where internal weaknesses coincide with external threats.
WT.primary_objective: Protect resources and deal quality by mitigating critical gaps, changing the pursuit approach, or reassessing viability.

tows_overrides.combination_policy: Generate only evidence-supported, contextually relevant combinations; do not force every possible factor pairing.

strengths.definition: Internal capabilities, assets, relationships, proof points, or execution advantages that can improve the seller's position in the specific opportunity.

factor_definitions.factor_description: A substantiated ability to connect the proposed solution to a material customer problem, measurable outcome, or strategic priority.
analytical_criteria: Verify quantified customer outcomes and the baseline used.
Distinguish customer-confirmed value from seller estimates.
Assess relevance to the customer's stated priorities.
evidence_expectations: Customer-confirmed business case or value model
Documented baseline and target metrics
Customer statements or records validating the value case

factor_definitions.factor_description: Demonstrable solution, technical, service, or delivery capabilities that address the customer's requirements.
analytical_criteria: Compare demonstrated capabilities with explicit decision criteria.
Verify relevant references, proof points, or validation results.
Separate demonstrated capability from roadmap or promise.
evidence_expectations: Requirements-to-capability mapping
Validated demonstration, pilot, reference, or delivery evidence
Technical or operational acceptance evidence

weaknesses.definition: Internal capability, evidence, relationship, positioning, or execution limitations that reduce the seller's ability to win or execute the opportunity.

factor_definitions.factor_description: Insufficient access, influence, or alignment across the stakeholders who shape, approve, fund, or implement the purchase.
analytical_criteria: Identify missing economic, executive, business, technical, procurement, and user stakeholders as relevant.
Test whether contact access translates into influence or decision access.
evidence_expectations: Stakeholder map and role evidence
Meeting records and customer-confirmed access
Decision authority and sponsorship evidence

factor_definitions.factor_description: The customer problem, business impact, funding, or commitment remains insufficiently validated to support a reliable win assessment.
analytical_criteria: Separate expressed interest from validated need and buying commitment.
Check baseline, impact, urgency, and funding evidence.
Identify unsupported assumptions and missing proof.
evidence_expectations: Customer-confirmed problem and impact
Budget or funding evidence where relevant
Documented customer commitments and milestones

opportunities.definition: External customer, market, project, operational, or decision conditions that may create a favorable path to value and selection.

factor_definitions.factor_description: An evidenced customer need, constraint, or improvement opportunity that the proposed solution may address.
analytical_criteria: Confirm the need is current and material to the customer.
Determine whether the need is funded, prioritized, or linked to a trigger.
Assess solution relevance without assuming purchase intent.
evidence_expectations: Customer statements and operational evidence
Business metrics or documented improvement targets
Trigger-event or strategic-priority evidence

factor_definitions.factor_description: An opportunity to establish meaningful differentiation through outcomes, capability, risk reduction, delivery, or commercial design.
analytical_criteria: Identify customer-valued decision criteria not adequately addressed by alternatives.
Test differentiation against incumbent, competitor, internal-build, and status-quo options.
evidence_expectations: Customer decision criteria
Competitive and alternative analysis
Validated differentiators and outcome evidence

threats.definition: External competitive, customer, procurement, funding, regulatory, timing, or execution conditions that may undermine the opportunity.

factor_definitions.factor_description: A credible external alternative, incumbent position, competitor advantage, or preference for no change that may prevent selection.
analytical_criteria: Identify actual alternatives and their influence.
Distinguish confirmed competitor facts from assumptions.
Assess switching barriers and status-quo consequences.
evidence_expectations: Customer-confirmed competitive landscape
Incumbent and alternative evidence
Decision criteria and competitive evaluation records

factor_definitions.factor_name: External Buying, Funding, or Execution Constraint
factor_definitions.factor_description: An external decision, procurement, funding, regulatory, timing, or implementation constraint that may delay or prevent the purchase.
analytical_criteria: Identify the source, owner, timing, and severity of the constraint.
Assess whether the constraint is confirmed, emerging, or hypothetical.
Determine impact on closeability and required mitigation.
evidence_expectations: Customer approval or procurement documentation
Funding, schedule, regulatory, or contractual evidence
Customer-confirmed dependencies and milestones

mandatory_considerations: Relevance to the customer's decision criteria and the current opportunity stage
Potential impact on deal quality, margin, and execution risk

prioritization_criteria: Prioritize gaps that could materially change factor classification, confidence, or strategic priority.
Prioritize evidence needed to resolve critical PADF, competitive, stakeholder, funding, and closeability uncertainties.
Request the smallest set of high-value evidence items that can change the decision or recommended action.

SO.strategic_logic: Use substantiated internal strengths to capture a relevant external customer or market opportunity.
SO.primary_objective: Convert proven capability and customer value into a differentiated, customer-validated path to selection.

WO.strategic_logic: Address a material internal weakness so the opportunity can be pursued credibly.
WO.primary_objective: Close evidence, capability, stakeholder, or execution gaps that currently prevent the opportunity from being converted.

ST.strategic_logic: Use substantiated internal strengths to mitigate or neutralize an external threat.
ST.primary_objective: Apply proven differentiation, relationships, technical capability, or delivery evidence to reduce competitive or buying-process exposure.

WT.strategic_logic: Reduce exposure where internal weaknesses coincide with external threats.
WT.primary_objective: Protect resources and deal quality by mitigating critical gaps, changing the pursuit approach, or reassessing viability.

combination_rules: Generate SO, WO, ST, and WT strategies only when the paired factors are relevant, current, and evidence-supported.
A strategy must cite the supporting SWOT factor IDs and evidence IDs.
Do not generate exhaustive combinations; prioritize combinations with material strategic relevance and feasible actions.
A single factor may support more than one TOWS strategy when the rationale and actions differ.
Do not treat a hypothesized factor as verified; strategy confidence must reflect the weakest material evidence dependency.
Assess feasibility, resources, execution timeframe, and expected winability impact before recommending a strategy.
